summary: Dedicated pool: evening P90 tail latency spikes and intermittent 504s due to GPU memory thrashing and autoscaler delay
description: Issue summary: Customer (ClipSync Media) reported a recurring spike in P90/P99 latency between 18:00-20:00 UTC over several days. Symptoms included ~30-40s queueing, elevated p95/p99 from ~180ms to 2.4s, and intermittent 504 responses for short requests. Impact: production traffic degradation for 3 customer-facing endpoints; increased error rates triggered PagerDuty. Environment: dedicated reservation (4xA10G per reservation) in us-west-2, model pinned to redwood/gpt-3-small-q4. Timeline: first observed 2026-03-08 evening, escalated 2026-03-10. Customer reported correlation with their evening batch traffic window.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Send sustained low-latency inference requests at 100 qps to the customer's reserved pool during 18:00-20:00 UTC window.
2) Simultaneously schedule an internal large-batch offline job that schedules long sequences/batched inference (simulated noisy neighbor).
3) Observe queue length, GPU mem usage, and p95/p99 token latencies.
4) Note autoscaler behavior when pool utilization crosses 70% (expected scale-up) and watch for cooldown delays.
Expected: steady latency ~ <250ms. Observed: long tail latency and intermittent 504s when noisy batch starts.

investigation_notes:
- Initial hypothesis: noisy neighbor batch jobs triggered GPU memory pressure leading to KV cache evictions and host staging for allocations, causing long tail token latencies and timeouts.
- Telemetry confirms repeated spikes in GPU memory usage to ~98% coincident with customer's reported window.
- Autoscaler logs show a scale-up decision at 18:09 but cooldown prevented immediate scaling due to a conservative cooldown policy from previous config.
- Confirmed internal background job (batch-analytics-job id=ba-2026-03-08) was scheduled in same cluster and used large micro-batches that preempted kernels.
- Kernel-level messages indicate cuMemAlloc fallback; this correlates with >30s latency windows and occasional 504s from api-gateway.
- Repro tested in staging by launching synthetic noisy neighbor with similar GPU batch characteristics; reproduced tail latencies and evictions.
- Considered model-level change (reduce batch size), autoscale policy modification, and tenant isolation via scheduling affinities.
comments: 2026-03-10 19:02 - Connor Blake (SRE): Running live traces now. I can see three sustained kernel preemption events at 18:06-18:12 that align with the spikes. Temporary mitigation: throttled internal batch job and bumped pool priority for ClipSync reservation.

2026-03-10 19:28 - María Gutierrez (Customer Success): Customer confirmed error rate dropped after throttling their nightly batch. They still saw elevated p95 for ~10 minutes after. Customer asks for long-term fix to avoid manual throttling.

2026-03-11 09:15 - Dylan Park (Autoscaler): Autoscaler cooldown was 120s; policy was inherited from a safety baseline. Proposed change: add burst_scale path that allows emergency scale-up for customer dedicated pools when memory-pressure metric > 90%. Will open PR with tests.

2026-03-11 15:47 - Connor Blake (SRE): Deployed temporary autoscale override in us-west-2 for ClipSync dedicated pool: cooldown reduced to 20s for emergency path and affinity rule applied to avoid scheduling offline batch pods onto reserved nodes.

2026-03-12 11:02 - Aisha Kapoor (Support): Customer validated evening window on 2026-03-11, no 504s and p95 returned to baseline after changes. Marking as resolved; follow-up actions in resolution section.
2026-03-12 11:05 - Engineering Lead (Ethan Li): Created follow-up epic to add kernel-level preemption backoffs and improve eviction telemetry. See CON-ENCAPS-721 for tracking.
2026-03-12 11:07 - Customer (ClipSync Ops): Thanks for fast response. Requesting recommendation doc to avoid future collisions between scheduled analytics and inference traffic.
resolution:
Immediate actions: 1) Throttled internal noisy neighbor batch job and applied node affinity to move analytics jobs off ClipSync reserved nodes. 2) Deployed autoscaler emergency path: reduced cooldown for emergency scale-ups when gpu_mem_pressure > 90%. 3) Increased eviction logging and alerting for KV cache evictions. 4) Short-term recommendation to customer: pin to smaller model variant during their batch window or schedule batches to off-peak.
Permanent/next steps: - Engineering to land autoscaler PR to safely allow faster emergency scaling for reserved pools (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/193). - Runtime team to add kernel preemption backoff and better host-staging mitigation. - Runbook update: document how to detect noisy neighbor and how to temporarily throttle internal batch jobs. Ticket closed after customer validation on 2026-03-11.
postmortem_actions: Add metric-driven scheduler isolation for dedicated pools
Improve KV cache eviction metrics and alerts
Customer-facing best-practices doc for scheduling large batches
customer_communication_summary: We acknowledged impact same day, provided immediate mitigation (throttling and affinity), and deployed autoscaler override. Customer validated fix within 24 hours and agreed to follow-up guidance on scheduling and model pinning.
notes_for_engineering: Link instrumentation traces: tracing.redwood.ai/trace/clip-584902 and GPU flamegraphs archived in s3://redwood-telemetry/clipsync/584902/. Consider adding adaptive preemption thresholds for workloads pinned to dedicated pools.
estimated_customer_impact: ~1.5 hours of elevated error rates during peak window across two days; temporary user-facing degradation for ClipSync endpoints affecting media sync tasks.
time_to_resolution: ~24 hours from escalation to full validation (2026-03-10 18:00 -> 2026-03-11 18:00)
business_risk: Medium - dedicated customer on paid reserved capacity; repeated incidents could lead to SLA credits if not prevented.
